title: From campus radicals to Beijing's AI sabotage: Rep Randy Fine says 'US fighting to save Western civilization'
summary: Florida Congressman Randy Fine on being an unapologetic defender of the MAGA agenda and the pressing need to emerge victorious against China in AI battle
story: In a wide-ranging interview, the Florida Republican ties domestic policy, campus protests, and data centers directly to foreign influence from Iran and China.
U.S. Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., has emerged as one of the most outspoken foreign policy voices in Congress during his short tenure on Capitol Hill.
He frames the modern political battleground not just merely as a domestic election but as an existential struggle to preserve Western civilization.

In a wide-ranging exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, the Florida Republican pulled no punches as he tied anti-Israel sentiment and opposition to domestic AI data centers directly to foreign influence operations by Iran and China, positioning himself as an unapologetic fighter for President Donald Trump’s agenda.
GOP REP RANDY FINE DECLARES THAT DEPORTING ALL ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS IS THE TOP WAY TO MAKE THE US AFFORDABLE
Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., leaves the U.S. Capitol after the last votes of the week on Sept. 4, 2025.  (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)

As the Israeli-Palestinian conflict has emerged as a political lightning rod, serving as a primary litmus test for the American left, Fine believes foreign money has played a large part in shaping public opinion.

"I think it's a focused effort over many decades to try to pollute our population with these ridiculous ideas," Fine said. "But I think it's accelerated since Oct. 7 as massive amounts of foreign money have come in to try and manipulate public opinion through social media. They lie. And here's how you know they lie. When other countries kill tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands of their people, no one seems to be bothered.

"But when Israel defends itself from a terrorist attack, they lose their minds. Iran killed 40,000 of its own people in a couple of days earlier this year. Those same people who are upset with Israel are actually siding with Iran. The good news is the vast majority of the American people understand that the United States and Israel are fighting to save Western civilization, and that's certainly a message that I'm focused on spreading every day."

As the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is sweeping through mainstream culture with the recent cancellation of Macklemore's tour dates in football stadiums, Fine is a staunch defender of Robert Kraft's decision and denies it's merely "conservative cancel culture."
Macklemore performs at St Anne's Park June 4, 2025, in Dublin, Ireland. (Redferns via Getty Images)

"So, first off, they weren't political statements," Fine said. "I mean, is calling for the death of Jews a political statement? I mean it's antisemitism in the same way racism against black people is. And while you're allowed to be an idiot, as this Macklemore guy is, you don't have the right to perform in a stadium that's owned by private citizens.
"He didn't want a guy who puts a prosthetic nose on his face, in order to appear to be a Nazi, performing in his stadium. He has every right to say that is not welcome.
"That doesn't mean Macklemore can't stand on the street corner and preach his views. Cancel culture is when you cannot exist, when you're debanked, when you literally cannot function in society.

"But in the same way, I have the right to say whatever I want, other people have the right to you can't say it in my house. And that's all that's happened here. I think he [Robert Kraft] did the right thing. I think we need more of it."
AOC JOINS MACKLEMORE FUNDRAISING MEMO TARGETING ROBERT KRAFT
Fine has also been at the forefront of condemning the militant pro-Palestinian protesters who have taken over university campuses across the country over the past year.

"I think we draw the line at violence. Every student has the right to get an education," Fine said. "And, so, for example, when Jewish students are not able to come to class, when they're not able to walk across campus, when they're blamed for the actions of a country on the other side of the world, that is where you've crossed a line.
Anti-Israel protesters demonstrate in New York city Oct. 5, 2024, ahead of the anniversary of the Oct. 7 Hamas attack. (Adam Gray for Fox News Digital)

"Look, I had to deal with the ‘free Palestine’ idiots when I was in college, you know, 30 years ago. But they didn't affect my ability to actually exist and to do my job and to be a student. So. I just didn't worry about it."
Fine has described himself as "MAGA through and through" and sees himself as one of the president's staunchest defenders in Congress.

"Well, I believe in making America great again. I've been a huge supporter of the president," Fine said. "I was the first member of the Florida House to support President Trump when he ran for president again in 2024. And I believe that the president is really putting his fingers in the dam of the destruction of Western civilization, which so many are trying to shove down our throats.
"So, I'm here to be a warrior and a soldier for President Trump's agenda, and I've been proud to do it since I got elected on April 1 of last year."

Virginia has long been at the center of America’s data center industry, with Northern Virginia now the largest data center market in the world and home to roughly 13% of global operational capacity. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

As domestic opposition to data centers has skyrocketed and AI regulation emerges as a major issue heading into the midterms, Fine warns that China is using both issues to win a geopolitical advantage over the United States.

"I think it's largely an op by China. And let's explain why. So, I think the 21st century, who wins the 21st century, will largely be defined by who wins the war over AI. And that fight is on four levels.
"One is hardware. Who has the best hardware? Right now, America is in the lead on that. Who has the best software? Right now, America is on the lead.

"Who has the best energy infrastructure? Unfortunately, China has the lead on that because while the idiots on our side have said let's not have coal-fired power plants … let's not have nuclear, let's get all of our energy from solar and windmills, China, who's selling us all the solar and the windmills, is putting up coal-fired power plants. So, cheap, plentiful energy. China's winning that fight.

"But the fourth front in that fight is what they call compute: data centers. If you want to use Grok, if you want to use ChatGPT, if you want to use Claude and you type that stuff in, something needs to be doing the thinking. It's not happening on your phone. It's happening at a data center. And China has realized that if they can get America to not put data centers in, well then those data centers have to go in China, and China wins on that front of the war.

"Does that mean you should be able to put a data center in a neighborhood? No, it doesn't. But does that mean the data centers are a critical part of re-industrializing the United States to make sure we win the war over AI? It absolutely is."
Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., speaks with union activists about free speech on college campuses at the Capitol in Washington May 23, 2024. (AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite)

Finally, Congressman Fine addressed the looming midterm elections as Republicans face headwinds to retain control of both chambers, making a forceful case for the GOP's accomplishments in the 119th Congress.

"Well, I'd say two things. No. 1, look at what we've done. The largest tax cut in American history. No tax on tips, no tax on overtime. Look at President Trump sealing the border. Look at the first net migration out of the country in decades. Look at the stopping of the transgender things. Look at all the extraordinary achievements. Remember how bad things were two years ago?
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"But the second thing is understand what we're at risk of if the Democrats win. All of the good things that we have done. Many of the Democrats that I serve with hate America. If you think Ilhan Omar, if you think Rashida Tlaib, if you think Abdulrahman Mohammed El-Sayed, if you think Zohran Mamdani, if you think they think America is good and that they love America, you're out of your mind.

"And the Democratic Party has been poisoned by people who hate America. The barbarians are no longer outside the gates, they're inside and they're running for Congress. And they can never be allowed to have power because they will make it their single-minded mission to destroy the country."
David Unsworth reports on Latin America. You can follow David Unsworth on Twitter @LatinAmerUpdate

title: Dem AG running for higher office dodges questions on bid to free man who killed pregnant woman
summary: Nevada AG and governor candidate, Aaron Ford, ducked questions about his decision to back early release for a man who killed a pregnant woman while out on bond for a series of other violent crimes.
story: Nevada's attorney general, who is also running for governor, sponsored the clemency application for a man convicted of killing a pregnant woman, then declined to answer questions when approached about the decision.

FIRST ON FOX: Nevada's Democratic Attorney General Aaron Ford is refusing to explain why he personally backed a clemency bid for a convicted killer who took the life of a pregnant woman while out on bail for a series of armed robbery attacks on Vegas tourists, dodging questions on camera as he campaigns to be the state's next governor.

State records in Nevada show Ford was listed as the sole sponsor for Norman Smith’s commutation application at a Sept. 16 Nevada Board of Pardons Commissioners meeting. Smith was serving time for killing a pregnant woman in a convenience store parking lot—a crime committed while he was out on bail for a series of armed robbery attempts committed against Vegas Strip tourists, according to court documents and local reporting at the time.

Despite Ford's backing, the board ultimately denied the clemency bid, while Ford skipped the commutation hearing that was scheduled and later walked away from a questioner asking him to justify the decision to sponsor Smith's application at a Las Vegas airport.
WHITE HOUSE DENIES TRUMP INFLUENCED BY 'PARDON BROKERS' AFTER '60 MINUTES' INVESTIGATION

Ford's sponsorship of the convicted killer's early release bid comes as he mounts a gubernatorial run against Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo, who has repeatedly attacked the attorney general's record on public safety and criminal justice reform.

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford smiles during his governor campaign kick off event at the East Las Vegas Community Center Monday, July 28, 2025, in Las Vegas. (Madeline Carter/Las Vegas Review-Journal)

When confronted about the sponsorship, Ford's campaign told Fox News Digital the attorney general missed the hearing due to an out-of-state family medical emergency and argued that sponsoring an application is merely a routine procedural step allowing the Board of Pardons to decide on a specific clemency request—but the campaign repeatedly refused to explain why Ford chose to elevate Smith's specific case.
"Are you Aaron Ford?" a conservative tracker asked the gubernatorial candidate as he deplaned in Las Vegas after flying to Arizona, the same day as Smith's Sept. 16 commutation hearing.
"I am," Ford replied to the tracker, who went on to tell the Nevada Attorney General that she has been "following his stuff" on social media. "Nice to meet you."
The tracker continued with small talk until pivoting to a question about the decision to sponsor Smith's clemency bid.
"I have a question, are you—you're sponsoring Norman Smith's pardon, right?"
BIDEN CLEMENCY BLITZ LEFT DOJ SCRAMBLING AS MANY COMMUTATONS BYPASSED NORMAL VETTING, EMAILS SHOW

"Uhh, don't know which one you're talking about, but anyway—good to see you," Ford responded before shuffling away with his wife following their trip to visit their college-aged son who was said to be sick. Fox News Digital pressed Ford's team on what his son was facing in terms of an ailment but was not provided an answer.
"Is there a reason why you're pardoning him?" Ford was asked as he attempted to skirt away from the questioner.
"Good to see you," was Ford's response before walking away. "Take care."
"No reason?" the tracker doubled down.
Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford and his wife are pictured at a Vegas airport departing their plane on Sept. 16, the same date as Norman Smith's clemency hearing. (Fox News.)
CALIFORNIA SUED OVER POLICY THAT COULD FREE SERIAL KILLERS AS LACI PETERSON'S FRIEND SOUNDS ALARM

Under Nevada Board of Pardons Commissioners rules, an inmate’s clemency application sits in a queue until one of the board’s nine members—which includes the governor, attorney general, and state Supreme Court justices—chooses to officially sponsor it. By sponsoring Smith’s application, Ford elevated the case out of the administrative queue and onto the official state agenda for a full hearing and vote.
Based on a Fox News Digital review of official meeting agendas from 2026, Smith’s application was the only commutation request sponsored by Ford all year.

In 2015, Smith was free on bail and facing 14 charges in connection with a series of armed robbery attacks on Vegas Strip tourists when he shot and killed the pregnant woman, Tineshea Adams, according to court documents and reporting at the time from the Las Vegas Review-Journal. Court documents show Smith, who was initially charged with murder but was eventually convicted of voluntary manslaughter and three counts of armed robbery, claimed the killing was the result of self-defense. Smith is currently serving a 10-to-39-year prison sentence.

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford speaks during his governor campaign kick off event at the East Las Vegas Community Center on Monday, July 28, 2025, in Las Vegas. (Madeline Carter/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)
Republican political strategist Matt Gorman slammed Ford's silent airport exit, telling Fox News Digital that the attorney general's refusal to answer speaks volumes.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Aaron Ford was moving faster through that airport than the violent criminals he’s trying to put back on the street," Gorman said. "If Nevada's top law enforcement officer can't even explain why he backed early release for a man who killed a pregnant woman while out on bail for a series of other violent crimes, he has no business asking voters to make him governor."
Following publication, Ford's campaign provided a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Attorney General Aaron Ford notified the pardon board that he had a family emergency last week and therefore had to miss the meeting," said Ford for Governor spokesperson Prerna Jagadeesh. "Joe Lombardo knew about the family emergency, and his campaign used it to attack Ford — that says a lot about Lombardo's character and the desperate campaign he's running. Pardon board members sponsoring clemency applications to check on the progress of an inmate is standard operating procedure and doesn’t mean a member will vote in favor of said application."
Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

title: Spanberger's data center plan on collision course with her party's green energy push, critics warn
summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger's data center plan restricts natural gas generation while demanding grid reliability, raising questions about the gap.
story: 'The Five' debate the growing backlash against artificial intelligence data centers over water and energy consumption. The co-hosts discuss President Donald Trump's defense of the facilities, warning that rejecting them is 'a mistake,' while Texas Gov. Greg Abbott warns companies they are digging their own graves due to power grid demands.
Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger's data center plan is facing criticism that one of its key provisions may work against itself.
Limits on on-site natural gas generation could make it harder, not easier, for large data centers to support Virginia's already-stressed electric grid.

The stakes are high because Virginia is already struggling to keep up with rapidly growing data center electricity demand, especially in Northern Virginia, where demand is outpacing the expansion of transmission lines and substations.

Restricting on-site natural gas generation could make it harder for large data centers to add dependable power at a time when the state is trying to stabilize the grid while also shifting toward cleaner energy sources.
WHO PAYS FOR US POWER BOOM? BLUE, RED STATES OFFER STARKLY DIFFERENT WAYS TO LOWER UTILITY BILLS AMID AI SURGE

"Everyone recognizes the need for changes in how Virginia engages with data centers. But the governor’s proposal is internally contradictory and raises serious questions about whether it can actually work," Virginia House Minority Leader Terry Kilgore told Fox News Digital.
Spanberger’s Data Center Accountability Framework calls for data centers to help stabilize the electric grid while limiting the amount of electricity they can generate from on-site natural gas.
Abigail Spanberger takes the oath of governor of Virginia during inaugural activities at the Capitol in Richmond, Va., Jan. 17, 2026. (Stephanie Scarbrough/AP)

Kilgore, R-Gate City, noted that the plan states data centers should source their "own clean power" while at the same time seeking to "limit the amount of electricity data centers can generate from … natural gas."
The plan also calls for accelerated clean energy development and prioritizes grid access for data centers that invest in "clean energy" or "further limit on-site natural gas generation."
"And if they fail to meet the governor’s preferred energy standards, they could face higher taxes," Kilgore said.
"What reliable, dispatchable source of power is supposed to fill the gap? That’s not a political question: it’s how the grid works."

A Spanberger spokesperson told Fox News Digital the governor's plan is the "most comprehensive and wide-ranging" in the country and that it aims to protect both Virginia residents and the commonwealth's "natural beauty."
"The governor’s plan also ends secrecy around data centers by banning non-disclosure agreements and strengthening local approval," the spokesperson said.

"While Gov. Spanberger is pushing to hold data centers accountable — an action polling shows is overwhelmingly supported by Democrats and Republicans — the Trump administration has continued to dismiss the very real concerns Virginians have about data centers’ energy, water and land usage."
Spanberger’s plan can still allow data centers to construct on-site power because the framework only restricts the use of that power.

She also signed a bill by Del. Rip Sullivan, D-Great Falls, that sharply increased Virginia's goals for energy storage, including a target of 1,600 megawatts of storage capacity at homes and businesses.
TEXAS GOV. GREG ABBOTT EFFECTIVELY PAUSES NEW DATA CENTER PROJECTS PENDING STATEWIDE GRID AUDIT

An Amazon Web Services data center in Stone Ridge, Va., July 28, 2024. Data center developers in Northern Virginia are asking utility Dominion Energy Inc. for as much power as several nuclear reactors can generate in the latest sign of how artificial intelligence is helping drive up electricity demand. (Nathan Howard/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Republicans said they found some common ground with Spanberger on the issue, citing public unease about the explosion in data center construction and stress on resources.

"I am glad the governor is finally talking about high power bills and data centers. Virginians already are," Senate Minority Leader Ryan McDougle, R-Hanover, said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital. "This should not be a partisan issue."
But he also echoed Kilgore’s concern about the plan’s energy-generation dynamics amid looming zero-emissions requirements.

"Virginians — Democrats, Republicans and Independents — will tell you the same thing. Their power bills went up. The laws raising electric bills — the tax on carbon, the Virginia Clean Economy Act, solar mandates, and more — should be repealed, and the companies building data centers should pay their own costs," McDougle said.
At the same time, some top Democrats criticized their governor’s plan.
"The governor is finally feeling the heat but still ignoring the fire," Senate President Pro-Tem L. Louise Lucas told Richmond’s ABC affiliate.
Lucas, Portsmouth, said the framework wrongly ignored the need to end tax exemptions for the centers.
The debate comes as Virginia is already in the midst of a state-mandated transition away from carbon-emitting electricity generation under the Virginia Clean Economy Act.

Under the law, the state’s major utilities generally must retire their remaining in-state generating units that emit carbon by burning fuel by the end of 2045. The law also allows utilities to seek relief from those requirements if compliance would threaten the reliability or security of electric service.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Spanberger’s new framework would push qualifying data centers further in that direction, limiting on-site natural gas generation while prioritizing grid access for facilities that invest in clean energy, reduce backup generator emissions and further restrict their reliance on natural gas.

Kilgore’s argument raised new tension. Restricting one source of on-site power before sufficient dependable alternatives are available could create the very reliability challenge Spanberger’s framework says it is intended to prevent.

The issue is particularly acute in Northern Virginia, where data center electricity demand is growing faster than the transmission lines and substations needed to serve it can be expanded, according to Loudoun County.

In Northern Virginia’s so-called data center alley, officials are already troubleshooting how to stabilize the grid as an explosion in data center construction puts massive sites among densely populated subdivisions.
There, Loudoun County leaders say the typical data center requires a continuous supply of 30 to 200 megawatts, enough to otherwise power 200,000 average homes.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Virginia has long been at the center of America’s data center industry, with Northern Virginia now the largest data center market in the world and home to roughly 13% of global operational capacity. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

The county’s explanation of data center development considerations also specifically lists "natural gas reciprocating engines" as one of the avenues for on-site power, appearing to contradict the push by the governor away from the fuel source.

Fox News Digital reached out to Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., for additional comment on the matter because he represents the county in Congress and has been a leading voice in the data center debate.

Earlier this month, Subramanyam introduced the National Data Center Plan, which would similarly require data centers to pay for their own energy, analyze their effects on the community, environment and national security before beginning construction.

The debate leaves the central dispute over Spanberger’s data center plan unresolved on whether clean generation, battery storage and flexible demand can provide enough dependable power to accommodate Virginia’s rapidly growing data center load as the state simultaneously restricts on-site natural gas generation.
Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Reporter's Notebook: Congress struggles to find a message that resonates with voters ahead of midterms
summary: Marshall McLuhan's "the medium is the message" frames a midterms fight where both parties struggle to sell voters on affordability and AI policy.
story: Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram reports on Democrats’ messaging ahead of the 2026 midterm elections and the debate over artificial intelligence regulation on ‘Special Report.’
Canadian sociologist Marshall McLuhan famously declared that "the medium is the message."
But what if the message is just "medium?" Or, perhaps in today’s vernacular, "mid."
Both sides are trying to curate what they say to voters to coax them to vote for their party in November.

"The message matters," House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., said on Fox. "We have accomplished a ton. No taxes on overtime. No taxes on tips. We raised the childcare tax credit. The list goes on and on."
EXCLUSIVE: INSIDE VANCE'S INTIMATE CAPITOL HILL HUDDLE AS REPUBLICANS CONFRONT TOUGH MIDTERM TERRAIN
House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., during a television interview at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., Sept. 30, 2025.  (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Those are all vestiges of the "big, beautiful bill," which the Republican-led Congress passed last summer. Now Republicans are scrambling to remind voters what they did.
"It was a great message last year, and we missed the opportunity, in my view, to talk about the good things we did last year," Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., conceded.
But Cramer says voters want to know what you’ve done for them lately. And that’s where the GOP could struggle.
"People's rearview mirror is getting shorter and shorter all the time," said Cramer. "What you are going to do for me today is more important to them than what you tried to do a year ago."
That’s why some Republicans are frank about their prospects at the polls.
"This midterm is going to be a f---ing bloodbath," fumed Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., who is retiring. "I think that both parties know everyone's putting blame on the Republicans right now."
Democrats are campaigning on affordability. The cost of groceries and fuel are top of mind.
"What's most important to Americans are pocketbook issues," said Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va. "And they see the tariff strategy as punishing our allies and punishing their pocketbooks for no purpose."
But Democrats are also stumping on a promise.
"The top priority in these next two years is going to be holding Donald Trump accountable," said Colorado Democratic House nominee Melat Kiros.
"We'll hold this administration accountable for its corruption," House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., warned.
"We will subpoena them if we need to," declared Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash.
It’s unclear if threats of presidential probes could dilute the Democrats’ directive this fall.
"When you talk about (investigations)," yours truly asked House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., "Does that step on your message in any way about costs?"

"No, because there's a cost to the American people around corruption," answered Jeffries. "Which is why the American people are demanding that action be taken and that we hold the crooks accountable."
FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., spoke during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol July 13, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)
Still, one Democrat says the party is better politically if it sticks to bread and butter issues.
"There are a lot of corruption questions," said Sen. Peter Welch, D-Vt. "But I think the gold ring, the brass ring, is focusing on affordability."
While Republicans try to remind voters about the "big, beautiful bill," another prominent GOP senator says his party lacks a coherent message.
"We're lucky because the Democrats don't have a plan either," said Sen. John Kennedy, R-La. "Here's the strategy for both sides. ‘The other guys are worse than me.’"
So, some Republicans are reverting to a wedge issue that worked for them at the ballot box two years ago.
"We're going to tell the story about the closed border. I mean, President Trump has the most secure border in our history," argued Sen. Katie Britt, R-Ala.
But both parties are evaluating a late-emerging issue: artificial intelligence.
"In the next 30 days, as we go into this election, Democrats have an opportunity to basically put AI on the ballot," Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., said on MS NOW.
Jeffries suggested Republicans are dismissing immediate concerns about AI agents going rogue.
"This is a serious thing. It requires urgent congressional action and Republicans are abandoning their responsibility," said Jeffries. "Democrats will not do that."
Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, faces a competitive race this fall in the Buckeye State. He tried to blend a sliver of concerns over AI with the "affordability" question last week.

The House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act, 417-3. The bill defrays the high utility costs consumers are sometimes forced to pay if they live near data centers. The legislation diverts those bills to Big Tech firms that run the data centers. So, Husted made the case to protect consumers from shelling out extra cash.
"If you create the cost, you should pay the cost," said Husted.
OBAMA PRIVATELY SOUNDS ALARM ON ‘DANGEROUS’ AI, URGES DEMOCRATS TO PUT ISSUE AT CENTER OF AGENDA
Data center development is surging across Texas, with North Texas taking the top spot in a new global ranking of the industry’s leading markets. (Yasuyoshi Chiba/Contributor/AFP/Getty Images)
But Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., the top Democrat on the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, stood in the way.

"It’s not enough for us to tell states to consider making data centers pay for grid updates rather than voluntary pledges or suggestions to states," said Heinrich. "Congress needs to pass real legislation with real teeth."

The New Mexico Democrat then objected, blocking Husted’s entreaty on the spot. However, Republicans actually think the move by Heinrich could boost Husted, help Republicans and backfire on Democrats. In other words, a Democratic blockade might assist the GOP make the point that they’re for affordability and the other party is standing in the way. Especially on a bill that passed with such overwhelming support in the House.
"Now there's a differentiation between Republicans and Democrats. Republicans are looking out for ratepayers. Democrats are not," said Cramer.

Fox is told it’s possible the Senate could try again on the data center-related measure before senators leave the Capitol for the midterms. Another on-the-spot, unanimous consent request would take a matter of minutes to either pass or block the bill (again).

But a customary debate accompanied by multiple procedural votes likely consumes a week — even if there’s support for the plan. That said, some lawmakers from both sides wouldn’t mind a roll call vote where they’re documented as supporting the issue. Or a vote where Republicans dare Democrats to go on the record opposing it.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

What that means is that the Senate likely leaves town for the midterms without addressing "affordability." Republicans can blame Democrats — a little. Specifically on the Ratepayer Protection Act. But Democrats aren’t in the majority. They can upbraid Republicans for not addressing some of those pocket book concerns.
That’s the "message" ahead of November. As Kennedy suggested, it might fall flat on both sides. Or, as is sometimes said these days, "mid."
After all, it is the midterms.
Chad Pergram currently serves as Chief Congressional Correspondent for FOX News Channel (FNC). He joined the network in September 2007 and is based out of Washington, D.C.

title: Red state Dem faces fury for suggesting illegal aliens should replace American workers
summary: Hallie Shoffner said farmers would "trade five Americans just for one" illegal immigrant worker, drawing sharp criticism from Sen. Tom Cotton's campaign.
story: Arkansas Democratic Senate candidate Hallie Shoffner claimed in a recent interview that a farmer told her ‘we’d trade five Americans for just one" illegal immigrant worker. (Credit: Free Arkansas via Youtube - Sept. 9)

A Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate from Arkansas is facing scrutiny for comments she recently made on a podcast suggesting that illegal alien workers are more valuable than their American counterparts.

"I want to talk about the fact that our immigration system is backlogged, bureaucratic and doesn't actually help anybody, including American employers who want folks who want to follow the law," Hallie Shoffner said on the "Free Arkansas Podcast" during an hour-long discussion about a wide spectrum of political issues.
Shoffner, a farmer, is running against Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark. in the deep red state.
DEM SENATE NOMINEE CHANGES TUNE ON ICE AFTER VOWING NOT 'ONE MORE DIME' FOR AGENCY

Left: Democratic Senate candidate Hallie Shoffner, who is running in Arkansas, is under fire for a recent comment suggesting that farmers prefer hiring illegal immigrants over Americans because of their work ethic. Right: Norman Greer, 84, and William Ballard (L) repair a grain table on Greer's farm as the threat of rain delays their plans to harvest soybeans on October 11, 2021 in Princeton, Indiana. (Ark. Agricultural Experiment Station, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons; Scott Olson/Getty Images)
She continued by saying she had a discussion with a fellow farmer, who she said was a Republican, about foreign labor.

"Labor is a huge issue, especially when you don't have a large workforce," she said. "And every farmer will tell you, 'yeah, at one point we did, or still do, employ undocumented immigrants.'" And it's absolutely ridiculous that these folks are being rounded up because they're hardworking people. They're some of the best people we know."
"And honestly, we'd trade five Americans just for one of them because of how hard they work," she said.

Shoffner then demanded a pathway for illegal aliens to work in the United States legally, claiming "when they're good workers, we pay them well, they're good workers, they spend money here [and] they have family here."
Cotton's campaign accused Shoffner of implying that she has hired illegal aliens.
OMAR'S NEW LEGISLATION TARGETING ICE SPARKS OUTRAGE WHEN THE INTERNET SEES WHAT'S IN IT: 'UN-AMERICAN'

"Hallie Shoffner’s campaign isn’t denying that she employed illegal aliens," campaign spokesman James Arnold told Fox News Digital. "They’re also standing by Hallie Shoffner’s claim that just one illegal immigrant is more valuable than five American citizens."
"Every Democrat running for Congress needs to answer if they agree with Hallie Shoffner’s belief that illegal aliens are worth more than Americans," Arnold said.

Sens. John Barrasso of Wyoming, Tom Cotton of Arkansas, Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia and James Lankford of Oklahoma attend a news conference following Senate Republican policy luncheons at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday, June 23, 2026. The Republican-led Senate voted to end the U.S. war with Iran, breaking with President Donald Trump on an unpopular foreign conflict that has raised Americans' cost of living, roiled markets and caused global economic fallout. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

In a response to Fox News Digital, Shoffner's campaign manager Anna-Lee Pittman said the candidate's comments were taken out of context, and accused Cotton of being unwilling to have a conversation to help "fix the immigration system."

Cotton, she said, "spends his days combing through video clips of Hallie Shoffner to find any possible inelegant phrase or line that he can chop up to misrepresent an hour-long conversation and present it with no context," noting that "[i]n this response, Shoffner relayed a conversation she had with another farmer about challenges with labor."
Shoffner once joined the chorus of left-wing calls to defund U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
DHS ISSUES SCATHING REBUKE AFTER FORMER ATLANTA MAYOR KEISHA LANCE BOTTOMS TOUTS CUTTING TIES WITH ICE

"I would vote to defund ICE as it exists right now," Shoffner said in an event June. "Immigration and Customs Enforcement was created not that long ago, and it no longer serves the purpose it was originally created for."

"I would not spend one more dime on ICE, because — not just because of the human dignity issue — but also the fact that it is now the largest law enforcement agency in the country," she said. "It has 10 times the budget of the organization that fights child sex trafficking."
Immigrant farmworkers harvest broccoli at a field in Brawley, California, on Dec. 10, 2024. (Sandy Huffaker/AFP via Getty Images)
But in a Facebook post earlier this month, the red state Democratic candidate changed her tune.
"I don’t want to defund ICE, I want to reform it," she said.
Immigration is a hotbed issue heading into the midterm elections, as it was two years ago during President Donald Trump's campaign to occupy the White House for a second term.
The Trump administration has carried out immigration operations nationwide to arrest and deport illegal aliens, drawing blowback from Democrat politicians and activists.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Fox News Digital's Alex Miller contributed to this report.
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Trump ally skips UNGA for first time — months after face-to-face with president gave way to bitter clash
summary: Giorgia Meloni's decision to skip the United Nations General Assembly follows an escalating public feud with Trump over G7 and NATO encounters.
story: President Trump and other world leaders deliver remarks as the UN General Assembly convenes in New York.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is not attending the United Nations General Assembly this week, an official confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Meloni’s decision not to attend breaks with a roughly 15-year stretch in which an Italian prime minister took part in the U.N. General Assembly’s annual high-level debate, according to Associated Medias, although the 2020 gathering was held largely virtually because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Meloni said she will not attend the UNGA, citing a packed schedule after attending six summits in three and a half weeks and saying she had "several dossiers" to handle at home.

Meloni’s absence also means the two leaders will avoid another face-to-face encounter after recent international summits put their growing tensions on public display, despite a previously warm relationship.
WORLD LEADERS DESCEND ON NEW YORK FOR UNGA — BUT WHO REALLY HAS AMERICA’S EAR?
President Donald Trump meets with Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in the Oval Office of the White House, Thursday, April 17, 2025, in Washington. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)

"We believe the United Nations the basic instrument for achieving peace everywhere. Indeed we want a stronger role United Nations, we are present at many initiatives and we have an Italian candidate at the helm of the FAO", Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said ahead of the summit, according to Italian outlet ANSA. "There is great attention from the Italian side."

Their spat escalated in June after Trump said Meloni had "begged" him to take a photo at the G7, months after tensions first surfaced publicly when Meloni opposed U.S. military action against Iran and called Trump’s criticism of Pope Leo XIV "unacceptable."
The two leaders have long had a warmer relationship than Trump has shared with many other U.S. allies, with Meloni notably the only European leader to attend his 2025 presidential inauguration.
In July, Meloni and Trump feuded in the lead up to the NATO summit in Turkey after Trump posted "RESTRAINING ORDER NEEDED," on Truth, alongside a photo of Meloni looking at him.
TRUMP-MELONI SPAT GROWS OVER CLAIM ITALIAN PM 'BEGGED' FOR PHOTO: 'ASTONISHED'
Meloni said Trump's statements were "completely made up" and that "neither I nor Italy ever beg." (Mandel NGAN / POOL / AFP via Getty Images; Bastien Ohier / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images))
"Trump's statements against Meloni speak for themselves," Tajani said in July while at a Sky TG24 event. "We are convinced that transatlantic relations go far beyond individual statements."
The exchange followed a June interview with Italy’s La7 after the G7, when Trump mocked Meloni over what he claimed was her eagerness to take a photo with him.

"She wanted a picture with me so ​badly. I wouldn't have taken it, but I felt sorry for her," Trump said at the time to La7 TV channel. "She's probably happy I talked to her. I didn't have to talk to her."

Meloni fired back: "I can only say it is disappointing that he does not show the same determination with the enemies of the West and of the United States, whose leaders he instead treats with far greater indulgence."
RUBIO TO VISIT ITALY, VATICAN AMID TROOP DRAWDOWN CALL, TENSION WITH TRUMP, POPE LEO: REPORTS
President Donald Trump publicly rebuked Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, accusing her of lacking "courage" and failing to support U.S. efforts against Iran. (Suzanne Plunkett/Pool/Reuters)
"There is one thing he should remember: neither I nor Italy ever beg," she added.
There have been looming tensions between the two leaders after Meloni distanced herself from the U.S. amid mounting domestic and political pressure over the widening Middle East conflict.
Trump also criticized Meloni for failing to assist the U.S. without letting U.S. forces use Italy's landing strips and runways, calling it "a great logistical inconvenience."

"She is doing poorly in Italy with her level of popularity, possibly because she turned down the United States of America, a Country that truly loves and protects Italy, when it came to denying Iran from obtaining or developing a Nuclear Weapon (But so did NATO, for that matter!)," he wrote in June.
TRUMP TAUNTS MELONI WITH FRESH PHOTO SALVO AS NATO SUMMIT PUTS ALLIES FACE-TO-FACE

European Council President António Costa, Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, French President Emmanuel Macron, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, US President Donald Trump, British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and European Union President Ursula von der Leyen pose for a family photo during the Group of Seven (G7) Summit at the Kananaskis Country Golf Course in Kananaskis, Alberta, Canada on June 16, 2025. (Photo by Ludovic MARIN / POOL / AFP) (Photo by LUDOVIC MARIN/POOL/AFP via Getty Images) (Getty Images)

Italy remains a key U.S. security hub in Europe, hosting nearly 13,000 active-duty American service members as of December 2025, according to Defense Manpower Data Center figures, with personnel based in Vicenza, Aviano, Naples and Sicily.

A senior administration official highlighted President Trump’s meetings with other heads of state and engagement with Gulf partners on Iran when asked by Fox News Digital about Meloni’s absence from the conference.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Tajani is expected to speak at the conference on Wednesday.
Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

title: White House to yank 750,000 fraudsters off ObamaCare, save taxpayers $2.2 billion, Vance says
summary: JD Vance says his White House Fraud Task Force will remove 750,000 fraudulent Obamacare recipients, saving American taxpayers $2.2 billion..
story: Taxpayers are saving billions as officials crack down on widespread healthcare program exploitation. The Fraud Task Force is stopping Obamacare enrollment for approximately 750,000 individuals suspected of fraudulent registration. Led by Secretary Kennedy and Dr. Oz, the coordinated effort also includes verifying the legal residency and income eligibility of 419,000 additional enrollees to ensure funds reach those in need.

Vice President JD Vance announced Tuesday that his White House Fraud Task Force will be removing 750,000 fraudulent Obamacare recipients from the program in an effort he says will save U.S. taxpayers $2.2 billion.
Additionally, the administration will be employing additional verification for another 419,000 people.

"We're going to make sure that they are, first of all, legal residents of the United States of America, and second of all, we're going to make sure that they actually meet the income threshold requirements in order to receive these Obamacare benefits," Vance said.

"To put into context the amount of money that we're stopping from going to fraudsters today, $2.2 billion, the average American child receives about $4,000 in health care benefits every single year. That means that we are saving 550,000 American children's worth of healthcare that was going to fraudsters and now will go to the essential services for which it was meant to go."
VANCE TO HOST CONGRESS AT WHITE HOUSE TO DISCUSS LEGISLATIVE ACTION ON FRAUD

U.S. Vice President JD Vance, flanked by Administrator for the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Dr Mehmet Oz and Chairman of the U.S. Federal Trade Commission Andrew N. Ferguson, accepts questions during a news conference on anti-fraud initiatives at the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on the White House campus in Washington, D.C. Sept. 22, 2026. (Reuters/Evan Vucci)

Vance criticized the administration of former President Joe Biden for incentivizing Obamacare fraud, arguing that the administration's incentives for brokers to enroll people in the program, combined with relaxed eligibility for the program, became the perfect recipe for rampant fraud.
WHITE HOUSE PUSHES 'WATERSHED' FRAUD-FIGHTING REFORM IN CONGRESS AS VANCE CONVENES TASK FORCE

"In one case we found a fraud ring that had 40 agents, 40 brokerage agents who had funneled 50,000 people into the Obamacare system fraudulently. Now, some of those people were probably legitimate. Most of those people were not eligible (because) either they didn't meet the citizenship or the income requirements. Many of those people quite literally didn't even exist."

Dr. Mehmet Oz, the administrator for the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and a member of Vance's Fraud Task Force, further expanded on the non-existent individuals fraudulently entered into Obamacare.
DR. OZ NAMES 5 STATES IN FRAUD CRACKDOWN AS TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS MEDICAID ABUSE
"Normally 1%, a single digit, 1% of people who get Obamacare exchange plans do not have a Social Security number," Oz said.

Vice President J.D. Vance, center, accompanied, from left, by Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Deputy Administrator & Chief Operating Officer Kimberly Brandt, Administrator for the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Dr. Mehmet Oz, Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson and Health and Human Services Deputy Secretary nominee Chris Klomp, speaks during a news conference on fraud at the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on the White House Campus Sept. 22, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

"We're supposed to check their tax returns to make sure they're making between one and four times the poverty level, so they're eligible for all of our taxpayers to pay their insurance so they get the discount. Now, if 100% of people coming on the program don't have Social Security numbers, I think we'd all agree there's a problem," he continued.
TRUMP ADMIN UNCOVERS 7,100% SURGE IN MEDICARE SKIN SUBSTITUTE CLAIMS, SAYS FRAUD CRACKDOWN BLOCKED MILLIONS
Oz then revealed that over 1.1 million people who enrolled in Obamacare this year had no Social Security numbers. He also revealed that 35% of enrollees have never used the program.

"They haven't bought a prescription medication. They haven't seen a doctor. That's just not possible. That's at least twice as much as your normal incidence of people having insurance and not using it. So, we know there is fraud," he added.
He then detailed the case of convicted fraudster Cory Lloyd, who he said has "a very punchable face."

Dr. Mehmet Oz, administrator for the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, speaks next to CMS Deputy Administrator and Chief Operating Officer Kimberly Brandt during a news conference on anti-fraud initiatives at the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on the White House campus in Washington, D.C., Sept. 22, 2026. (Reuters/Evan Vucci)

Lloyd and his partner, Stephen Strong, preyed on vulnerable consumers to enroll them in Obamacare in a scheme to collect commission payments from insurance companies, according a February announcement from the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ).
"These crooks bribed homeless and jobless people into enrolling in the ACA plans. They had no idea what they were doing," Oz said.
Oz read text messages between Lloyd and Strong in which the pair schemed to enroll people who had lost their homes from hurricanes in Florida.

"This is the text message. This is ... I can't even say these words on television. But Lloyd said 'it's a killer idea to sign up these poor individuals, make them victims. If it could pull it off. I want to rape the shelters.' And then Strong said, 'ha ha, not kidding. And then Lloyd said 'me either. Let's ef 'em up,'" Oz relayed.

Vice President J.D. Vance, center, appears onstage as Deputy Administrator & Chief Operating Officer Kimberly Brandt  holds up a poster depicting a text conversation with Cory Lloyd, convicted of Affordable Care Act fraud, as Administrator for the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Dr. Mehmet Oz, right, speaks during a news conference on fraud at the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on the White House Campus Sept. 22, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

The pair were both convicted of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, three counts of wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, according to the DOJ. Strong was also convicted of two counts of money laundering. Both were sentenced to a total of 20 years in prison and ordered to pay $180.6 million in restitution, according to the DOJ announcement.

Fox News Digital contacted the DOJ and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services for further comment.

title: Federal indictment handed down in Minnesota related to issue some Dems claim never happens: 'Hotbed for fraud'
summary: Mukeshkumar Chaudhari, an Indian national, faces a federal indictment for falsely claiming U.S. citizenship to vote in Minnesota's 2024 election.
story: Federal prosecutors charged a Honduran national with voter fraud in California after he allegedly registered to vote under an alias and cast ballots in multiple elections. Fox News' Matt Finn reports on the federal indictment details, revealing the suspect received a voter registration card using a gym membership. The case highlights ongoing debates surrounding voter identification laws.

An Indian national was federally indicted by a grand jury in Minnesota for knowingly making the false claim to be a U.S. citizen to vote in the 2024 general election, prompting pushback online and from an expert who spoke to Fox News Digital.

Mukeshkumar Somabhai Chaudhari, according to a DOJ press release earlier this month, falsely claimed U.S. citizenship by signing a voter signature certificate required under state law to vote in Minnesota and voting Nov. 5, 2024.

"The right to vote is a sacred privilege of American citizenship, and every lawful voter deserves an election system in which that right is protected," Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division said in the press release.
MN DEM SENATE CANDIDATE'S VIRAL HIJAB VIDEO TAKES NEW TURN AS WOMAN BESIDE HER FACES MAJOR STATE INVESTIGATION

"The Department will hold accountable those who knowingly make false claims of citizenship in order to vote. The integrity of our elections depends on ensuring that only eligible citizens cast ballots and that every lawful vote is counted."
Dhillon added in a post on X Tuesday that the Justice Department has "indicted or convicted 67 individuals for election related crimes."

Earlier this year, Fox News Digital reported that Chaudhari, 39, was facing state perjury and voting violation charges and that he denied he voted when first questioned by authorities but later claimed he "made a mistake" and admitted to voting while also telling investigators he is not a U.S. citizen.
Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz met with Trump border czar Tom Homan as the administration reshuffled federal immigration leadership in the state. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Chaudhari, according to investigators, received a voter registration notice from the state of Minnesota in a move that was likely triggered in the system after he obtained his driver’s license. Chaudhari is said to have told authorities that he didn’t learn he should not have voted until his lawyer informed him during his green card process.

"Once again, DOJ is proving that if you look for election fraud, you find election fraud," Chad Ennis, vice president of Honest Elections Project, told Fox News Digital Tuesday. "The left loves to claim election fraud does not happen. But here we have yet another instance of a noncitizen illegally registering to vote."
News of the federal indictment spread across social media as well, with some users pointing out that numerous elected Democrats in recent years have downplayed the existence of voter fraud.
"That thing that never happens," Center for the American Experiment’s Bill Glahn posted on X.
DEMOCRAT NEW JERSEY GOVERNOR SAYS THOUSANDS OF NONCITIZENS DISCOVERED ON VOTER ROLLS, PURGED
"Tim Walz's Minnesota is a hotbed for fraud!" political commentator Eric Daugherty posted on X.

Glahn previously spoke to Fox News Digital about his concerns over the lack of safeguards in Minnesota’s voting system, including registered voters being able to "vouch" for up to eight other voters’ residency who want to sign up for same-day voter registration without an ID.
"Only U.S. Citizens are eligible to vote in Minnesota," the Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State told Fox News Digital earlier this year, adding that ineligible voting is "extremely rare."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A polling place  (Adam Gray/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"When an individual completes a voter registration application, they attest that they meet all eligibility requirements, including that they are a U.S. citizen," the office said. "Before casting a ballot, one must again swear to their eligibility before they are allowed to vote.

"If a noncitizen attempts to vote in an election, they will be caught and held to account. Penalties for voting while ineligible may include deportation, a permanent bar on future citizenship, a fine of up to $10,000, and up to five years in prison."
If convicted, Chaudhari faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison on each of the two counts he faces.
Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter at Fox News. Find him on Twitter @andymarkmiller and email tips to AndrewMark.Miller@Fox.com.

title: Mamdani blasts DoorDash CEO's 'greedy algorithm,' NY slaps company with $131 million settlement
summary: Zohran Mamdani announced a historic $131.5 million DoorDash settlement over alleged systematic underpayment of food delivery workers in New York City.
story: Following an investigation into 152 million payments, New York City secured a landmark $131 million settlement with DoorDash for violating minimum pay standards. More than 260,000 delivery workers who were underpaid between April 2022 and June 2026 will receive direct payments starting in late October. The food delivery giant must also submit compliance data for three years.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani blasted DoorDash CEO Tony Xu for encouraging the use of a "greedy algorithm" while announcing the city's historic $131 million settlement with DoorDash over discrepancies in the company's pay to drivers

"Two months ago, Tony Xu, the CEO of DoorDash, gave business owners a piece of advice. A CEO, he said, has to take the greedy algorithm and keep going all the way to see if there is more," Mamdani said during a Tuesday news conference, recalling remarks Xu made on a podcast released in July.

"In computer science, a greedy algorithm is one that makes the most optimized, best short-term outcome choice at every step and never weighs the consequences. New York City and the tens of thousands of delivery workers who call our city home have reckoned with greed as a business model for far too long," Mamdani continued.
"Thousands of them deliver for DoorDash, and thousands of them have felt the human cost of the greedy algorithm," he added.
DOORDASH DEACTIVATES DRIVER ACCUSED OF STEALING DHS FOOD ORDERS AFTER VIRAL POST
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani at a press conference defending worker rights for delivery-app drivers on Jan. 15, 2026. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

At the news conference, Mamdani announced a historic $131.5 million settlement between DoorDash and the city of New York after the city's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) discovered that the company was systematically underpaying delivery drivers.
Mamdani said the $131.5 million marked the "largest settlement for food delivery workers ever secured in American municipal history."

From the settlement, $115 million will go directly back to delivery workers, with some in line to receive up to $5,000. The rest will go toward fines and the development of software that will allow delivery workers to record the DoorDash app and share data about their payment with the city.
DOORDASH GETS FAA APPROVAL FOR ITS OWN DELIVERY DRONES
"For the first time, workers will have the power to crowdsource data and investigate the black box algorithms that dictate their schedules and pay," Mamdani announced.
Under the settlement, DoorDash will also be required to regularly submit delivery worker payment data to the city for three years.
AMERICA’S TIPPING CULTURE HAS GONE FROM REWARDING SERVICE TO FEE INSANITY
A delivery person for DoorDash rides his bike in the rain in the Manhattan borough of New York City on Nov. 13, 2020. (Reuters/Carlo Allegri/File Photo)
AMERICANS SAY TIPPING PRACTICES 'HAVE BECOME RIDICULOUS' AS DIGITAL PROMPTS PUSH HIGHER GRATUITIES
DoorDash admitted to underpaying workers, though claimed it was unintentional.
"Simply put, we screwed up," DoorDash said in a statement obtained by the Associated Press.

"While these mistakes weren’t intentional, that doesn’t make them okay. We pride ourselves on operational excellence at DoorDash – and this was not excellent, nor was it acceptable. Dashers should be paid in full, on time, every time. We are sorry to the Dashers we let down," the company said.
But while the company characterized the underpayments as a slip-up, Mamdani said the company's alleged misconduct was no accident.
MAMDANI TURNS ON NEW YORK CITY TEACHERS UNION WITH LAWSUIT BLOCKING PAY RAISES FOR EDUCATORS

"For years, DoorDash failed to count every hour worked by delivery workers. This was not a rounding error or an accidental mistake. In 2023, when the city began enforcing a minimum pay rate for delivery workers, DoorDash left time out of the count, time on canceled trips and trips that crossed city limits," he said Tuesday.
Fox News Digital contacted DoorDash for further comment on Mamdani's remarks.
AMERICA NEEDS TO STOP TURNING EVERY PURCHASE INTO AN UNCOMFORTABLE TIP REQUEST
In this photo illustration, a person demonstrates making a delivery with DoorDash on April 2024, in San Francisco, California. (Emily Dulla/Getty Images for DoorDash)
Mamdani's announcement marks the latest in his ongoing crusade against food delivery conglomerates.

In January, he announced a $5 million settlement with a group of companies that included Uber Eats for failing to pay drivers minimum wage. In April, his administration secured a $875,000 settlement with HungryPanda for allegedly charging area businesses illegal junk fees.
